newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen slightly lower at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen slightly lower at open.

text.p: Wall Street shares were expected to open mixed to slightly lower on Wednesday, as the recently-strong technology stocks eased and blue chips struggled for air in a higher interest rate environment.

Technology stocks, whose gains have underpinned the broader stock market this week, could suffer profit-taking after giant networking equipment maker Cisco Systems Inc reported earnings which were in line with Wall Street forecasts but below the so-called "whisper" numbers.
The Dow industrials would also have a tough time advancing, given softness in the bond market, analysts said.

"The Cisco results might put some pressure on the over-the-counter market," Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said. "Plus, the bond market is weaker. Initially, we are probably headed for a lower open which could reverse later in the day."
Cisco, the world's biggest maker of computer networking gear, posted fourth quarter earnings of $0.55 per share versus $0.42 per share in the year-ago quarter.
The results were in line with Wall Street estimates but below unpublished forecasts, which traders said ran as high as $0.60 per share. The stock dipped in after-hours trading.
"Weakness in Cisco may cause the techs to give back some of their trading gains," Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co, said.
Rising yields in the bond market would also hamper stock market gains because richly-valued blue chip shares preferred a lower interest rate outlook, analysts said.
In early trade, the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index fell 0.90 point to 955.60, as the long bond lost 4/32 to yield 6.50 percent.
"Weakness in the bond market should cause the Dow to move in a more restrictive trading range," Cardillo said.
The Dow would track bonds even though the bond market's near-terms concerns centered on supply and upcoming Treasury auctions, rather than on inflation, analysts said.
"Bonds are focused on a $12 billion auction of 10-year notes," Ackerman said. "The market also has to get through the Beige Book data this afternoon."
The Federal Reserve would issue its Beige Book of economic conditions at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT. Analysts said bonds would react to clues on economic conditions in different regions.
Ackerman also said some concern was creeping into markets about the impact of an ongoing strike at U.S. courier company United Parcel Services of America.
In other markets, the dollar softened against the yen, trading at 119.10/20 yen. In Europe, the dollar set a new high against the mark, then traded at 1.8866/71 marks.
Japan's Nikkei average closed up 187.62 points, or 0.96 percent, at 19,702.07.
In London, the FTSE 100 was up 45.0 at 5005.6.
U.S. stocks were mixed in quiet London trading.
The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column that analysts are debating whether retail stocks can manage to hold gains in the second half of the year.
The New York Times said in its Market Place column that a new tax law signed on Tuesday by President Clinton could create large tax bills for Estee Lauder and her son Ronald.
